class MatchTier(str, Enum):
    """How the value was found, from strongest evidence to weakest."""

    EXACT = "exact"              # verbatim in the source

def match_number(
    value: Any,
    source: str,
    *,
    tolerance: Decimal | None = None,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a numeric value, regardless of how it is formatted in the source.

    This is where most naive grounding checks fail: the model returns
    ``4500.0`` and the document says ``$4,500.00``. Comparing parsed values
    rather than strings is the only way to get this right.
    """
    if is_trivial(value):
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    target = parse_number(str(value))
    if target is None:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value is not numeric")

    # Verbatim first, so an exact textual match still reports as EXACT.
    raw = str(value)
    exact_spans = _find_all(source, raw)
    if exact_spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, exact_spans[:5])

    matches: list[Span] = []
    near: tuple[Decimal, Span] | None = None

    for raw_text, start, end, found in iter_numbers(source):
        if found == target or tolerance is not None and abs(found - target) <= tolerance:
            matches.append(Span(start, end, raw_text))
        else:
            delta = abs(found - target)
            if near is None or delta < near[0]:
                near = (delta, Span(start, end, raw_text))

    if matches:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.SEMANTIC, 1.0, matches[:5],
            note="numeric value present, formatted differently",
        )

    note = "no matching number in source"
    if near is not None:
        note = f"nearest number in source is {near[1].text!r}"
    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, 0.0, note=note)

def match_text(
    value: str,
    source: str,
    *,
    fuzzy_threshold: float = 0.85,
    window_slack: float = 0.35,
) -> Match:
    """Locate a string value in the source document."""
    if not value or value.strip().casefold() in _TRIVIAL:
        return Match(MatchTier.NONE, note="value too trivial to verify")

    # Tier 1: verbatim.
    spans = _find_all(source, value)
    if spans:
        return Match(MatchTier.EXACT, 1.0, spans[:5])

    # Tier 2: same after folding unicode, whitespace and case.
    norm_source = normalize_text(source)
    norm_value = normalize_text(value)
    if norm_value and norm_value in norm_source:
        idx = norm_source.find(norm_value)
        start = _map_to_original(source, idx)
        end = min(len(source), start + len(value))
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.95,
            [Span(start, end, source[start:end])],
            note="matched after whitespace/case/unicode normalisation",
        )

    # Tier 2b: punctuation-insensitive. Catches "Acme, Inc." vs "Acme Inc".
    stripped_source = strip_punctuation(norm_source)
    stripped_value = strip_punctuation(norm_value)
    if stripped_value and stripped_value in stripped_source:
        return Match(
            MatchTier.NORMALIZED, 0.9,
            note="matched ignoring punctuation",
        )

    # Tier 4: fuzzy, over a sliding window sized to the value.
    best = _best_fuzzy_window(value, source, norm_value, window_slack)
    if best and best[0] >= fuzzy_threshold:
        score, span = best
        return Match(
            MatchTier.FUZZY, score, [span],
            note=f"closest text in source is {score:.0%} similar",
        )

    return Match(MatchTier.NONE, best[0] if best else 0.0)

def parse_date(raw: str, *, day_first: bool | None = None) -> _dt.date | None:
    """Parse a date written in any common human format.

    ``day_first`` disambiguates ``03/04/2026``. Left as ``None`` the ambiguous
    case is only resolved when one reading is impossible (a value above 12),
    and otherwise returns ``None`` rather than guessing, because a silently
    wrong date is worse than an unverified one.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    for pattern, kind in _DATE_PATTERNS:
        m = pattern.search(s)
        if not m:
            continue
        try:
            if kind == "ymd":
                return _dt.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
            if kind == "dmy_or_mdy":
                first, second, year = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
                if first > 12 and second <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if second > 12 and first <= 12:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                if day_first is True:
                    return _dt.date(year, second, first)
                if day_first is False:
                    return _dt.date(year, first, second)
                return None  # genuinely ambiguous; refuse to guess
            if kind == "dmonthy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(2).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(1)))
            if kind == "monthdy":
                month = _MONTHS.get(m.group(1).lower().rstrip("."))
                if month:
                    return _dt.date(int(m.group(3)), month, int(m.group(2)))
        except ValueError:
            return None  # e.g. 31 February
    return None

def parse_number(raw: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a human-written number into a Decimal.

    Handles currency symbols, thousands separators in either convention,
    and accounting-style negatives written as ``(1,234.00)``.

    Returns ``None`` rather than raising, because unparseable text is an
    expected input here, not an error.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return None
    s = fold_unicode(str(raw)).strip()
    if not s:
        return None

    negative = False
    # Accounting negatives: (1,234.56)
    if s.startswith("(") and s.endswith(")"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:-1].strip()

    # Strip currency symbols and codes
    s = re.sub(r"[" + re.escape(_CURRENCY_SYMBOLS) + r"]", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:USD|EUR|GBP|PKR|INR|JPY|AED|SAR|CAD|AUD)\b", "", s, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    s = s.replace(" ", "").replace("\u00a0", "").strip()

    if s.startswith("-"):
        negative = True
        s = s[1:]
    elif s.startswith("+"):
        s = s[1:]

    if not s or not re.search(r"\d", s):
        return None

    # Resolve separator convention by the position of the last separator.
    last_comma = s.rfind(",")
    last_dot = s.rfind(".")

    if last_comma > last_dot:
        # European: dots are thousands, comma is decimal
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    elif last_dot > last_comma:
        # US: commas are thousands, dot is decimal
        s = s.replace(",", "")
    else:
        # Only one kind of separator present, or none.
        sep = "," if last_comma >= 0 else ""
        if sep:
            parts = s.split(",")
            # "1,234" -> thousands. "12,34" -> decimal (2-digit tail).
            if len(parts[-1]) == 3 and all(len(p) <= 3 for p in parts):
                s = s.replace(",", "")
            else:
                s = s.replace(",", ".")

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d*\.?\d*", s) or s in {"", "."}:
        return None

    try:
        value = Decimal(s)
    except InvalidOperation:
        return None
    return -value if negative else value
